subject: Discrepancy: repeated token billing after outage — credits & timeline
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam@pilotanalytics.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spike on June 14 invoice — looks like duplicate billing

Jonas —

We just opened our June invoice and see a large spike in billed tokens between 23:05–23:18 UTC on Jun 14. Our accounting team flags this as a likely duplicate counting event (same session IDs repeated). Attached is the invoice extract (invoice-20270615.pdf) and a short sample of the session IDs we pulled (usage-excerpt.csv).

Can you confirm if this was caused by the outage you had last night? If so, what is Redwood’s plan for credits/refunds and timeline? We need an amount to book as a receivable adjustment this week.

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation.

Sam Carter
Head of Product
PilotAnalytics
Attachments: invoice-20270615.pdf (pdf), usage-excerpt.csv (csv)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:40:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Sudden spike on June 14 invoice — needs credit calc and ops response

Team — forwarding PilotAnalytics. Sam included a sample; they’re seeing repeated session IDs clustered during our autoscaler rollback window. Can we get: 1) quick RCA note we can share with customer, 2) proposed credit amount (dollars and token count) and whether we apply to next invoice or issue immediate refund, 3) artifacts (corrected invoice + attestation).

Quick context: Ops ran a rollback at 23:04 UTC to mitigate a controller bug that caused duplicate request retries. Early signal suggests KV-cache flush + retry happened for some sessions which resulted in double-counting of tokens for replayed requests. I need a conservative credit plan we can promise today.

Please @ben: compute the duplicate-token estimate from the sample and propose $ credit. @marissa / @monica: draft the customer-facing RCA language I can send. @neha: confirm SLA/contract constraints (any cap) and if we need approval to issue a one-time credit.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
Internal attachments: usage-excerpt.csv

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:03:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden spike on June 14 invoice — credit calc

Jonas / Marissa — quick calc from the sample:
- Sample shows ~1,220 duplicated requests totaling ~1.8M tokens duplicated during the 13-minute window.
- Using PilotAnalytics rate (hosted tier) at $0.0025 per 1k tokens => duplicate charge ~ $4,500.
- Suggestation: issue a one-time credit for 100% of the duplicated token charges ($4,500) applied to next invoice, or offer immediate refund if they prefer. We should include corrected invoice + a short attestation note.

Attached: credit_calc_20270615.xlsx (spreadsheet stub).

Ben Carter
Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachments: credit_calc_20270615.xlsx

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sam Carter <sam@pilotanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@pilotanalytics.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden spike on June 14 invoice — credits & timeline

Sam — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. Short summary and next steps below.

What happened
On Jun 14 at ~23:04 UTC we performed an emergency rollback of a controller change intended to address an unrelated performance regression. During the rollback an internal retry path was briefly re-enabled while KV cache invalidation completed. That combination caused a subset of in-flight requests to be retried and recorded twice in our metering pipeline, leading to inflated token counts for affected sessions. Our engineering team has deployed a fix to ensure retries are idempotent and added additional guards on the metering window.

Our proposed remediation
- Credit: Redwood will apply a one-time credit of $4,500 to PilotAnalytics’ next invoice to cover the duplicated token charges identified in the sample.
- Corrected invoice: attached is a corrected invoice that removes the duplicated tokens (corrected-invoice-20270615.pdf).
- Attestation: we’ll include a short attestation describing the engineering fix and the scope of affected sessions; full logs can be shared under an NDA if you need deeper audit evidence.
- Refund option: if you prefer an immediate refund instead of a credit, reply with the last 4 digits of the account for ACH and we’ll process it within 5 business days.

Timeline and next steps
- Today: We will apply the credit to your account and send the corrected invoice (attached).
- By EOD Jun 16: Ops will provide a short RCA note suitable for your procurement team.
- If you need a signed attestation or additional audit logs, we can get that to you in 48–72 hours upon NDA.

Apologies again for the impact — we take metering accuracy seriously and have added extra checks to prevent recurrence. Please confirm which option you prefer (credit applied to next invoice or immediate refund) and whether you want the attestation shared with procurement.

Best —
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199
Attachments: corrected-invoice-20270615.pdf
